chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn Salamah al-Kūfī, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a slave who killed four free men, one after another. He said: “He belongs to the family of the last of the slain; if they wish, they may kill him, and if they wish, they may enslave him. That is because when he killed the first, his heirs became entitled to him. Then when he killed the second, he was taken from the heirs of the first and became for the heirs of the second. Then when he killed the third, he was taken from the heirs of the second and became for the heirs of the third. Then when he killed the fourth, he was taken from the heirs of the third and became for the heirs of the fourth; if they wish, they may kill him, and if they wish, they may enslave him.”

key_terms.أَحْرَارٍ: free persons, in contrast to a slave
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: his heirs or legal claimants entitled to retaliation or disposition
key_terms.اسْتَرَقُّوهُ: they took him as a slave
key_terms.اسْتُحِقَّ: he became claimed as a legal entitlement
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave; the offender discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave kills several free men one after another?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a slave who kills multiple free persons in succession. It states that the right over him passes to the heirs of the most recent victim, who may either execute him or take him as a slave, because each subsequent killing transfers the claim from the earlier heirs to the later ones.
